topic: What a completed MCP-to-CLI transport decommission teaches: which failures were latent and why, what classes of residue a transport removal leaves behind, and what a repeatable checklist for the next such migration would contain.
label: deepseek-research

focus: The latent-failure class: a path that only runs after another has already failed
noveltyJustification: The class was named by the prompt, but the three-property structure, the HEAD-verified membership list, the provenance result that promotion converts exposure zero into exposure one, and the five-site alias duplication defect are new to this packet's record.

ruledOut.approach: Explaining the flat socket probe as a mistyped or stale literal
ruledOut.reason: The bridge scopes the default socket directory by construction, so the literal was the correct unscoped form; only a single-owner fix generalises

ruledOut.approach: Treating a distinguishable fallback reason code as sufficient observability
ruledOut.reason: socket_absent is in RETRYABLE_REASONS, so the caller treats it as expected

graphEvents.label: Fallback-only path fails latently via order-gating, unverified preconditions and masked failure
Env alias chain renamed into a duplicate operand at five sites
Which promotion-time checks would have failed for each member?

focus: The detection surface: which checks would have failed at promotion time, and in what cost order
noveltyJustification: New content is the seam-scoping explanation for three green harnesses missing the cluster, the seven-check cost ladder mapped to members, the counter-example proving a literal assertion would have passed on the defective revision, and the pre-flight-probe amplification mechanism.

ruledOut.approach: Widening the parity harness to cover the hook helper
ruledOut.reason: Its allowlist encodes genuine surface differences, so covering the seam requires modelling its semantics; a cross-seam equality assertion is smaller and sufficient

ruledOut.approach: A test asserting the helper's socket path literal
ruledOut.reason: The defective revision's own output is what the literal test would assert, so it cannot catch the premise error

graphEvents.label: Component-scoped harnesses leave the composition unowned
Seven checks ordered by cost; only invocation inversion has a proven catch
Value assertions re-encode the premise; only owner comparisons are independent
A local pre-flight probe amplifies a premise error into a short-circuit

focus: Residue inventory: the seven classes, their carriers, and the instrument that found each
noveltyJustification: The class structure, the documentation-that-died-inside-the-deleted-block sub-class, the measured 603-reference cross-package remainder with distribution, the lying-name versus live-vocabulary distinction, the present-tense-diagnostic distinction and the outside-the-corpus class are all new to this packet's record.

ruledOut.approach: Treating name residue as one class closed by a token sweep
ruledOut.reason: mcpServerDir and the mcp trigger aliases share the token and need opposite dispositions

ruledOut.approach: A blanket regenerate-after-rename step for generated artifacts
ruledOut.reason: One generator run rewrote 18,966 unrelated lines and shifted advisor scores; the manifest generator fails on an unrelated resolution defect

graphEvents.label: Seven residue classes, each needing a different instrument

Which classes does tooling find, and which require reading?

focus: Tooling versus reading: the search-key property, and the pre/post-removal split
noveltyJustification: R8 as a class, the in-repo contrast with the working LEGACY_ALIASES table, the correction that two live documents inside the swept tranche still assert the dead alias, the restatement of the split as a property of the search key, the availability-then-cost scheduling rule, and the handoff-without-acceptance class are all new to this packet's record.

ruledOut.approach: Treating the env-in-block residue as a post-deletion search
ruledOut.reason: The deleted block's contents are not in the tree at all; the instrument is git history, so the class is a pre-deletion read

ruledOut.approach: Treating the seven-class taxonomy from iteration 3 as closed
ruledOut.reason: R8 appeared only when the split forced the question of what search key each class needs

graphEvents.label: The tooling-versus-reading split is a property of the search key
